rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the cited revert commit `648ca4e8f6` (plan.html:371) is a review-record commit; the reversion is `195e7a80ac`, an ancestor of the cited commit, so the pointer lands on the right tree but names the wrong commit for the event.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §22's boundedness arm (plan.html:371) states no figure and no tolerance for "the station's resident memory and tick time", and the observation it names is an hour on the live station, which the node that builds it cannot run.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §22 cites no scratch path, and the gate logs of its reader arm sit on the run's durable evidence directory; the missing record behind the station observation is the done_when finding, not a path defect here.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new clause names no plan label, stage name or ticket number; the commit hashes it cites stay in plan prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the revert body of `195e7a80ac` supports the root cause s22 now states ("every ledger load decode the whole 797 MB run store", and the follow-up "stats about 11,000 run files on every load: the station reached 8.6 GB and a full core"), and the endpoint drawn from it — neither decode the whole store nor stat the whole runs directory — addresses both measured failures.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §22 now carries two deliverables: the reader-equality measure a suite can close, and a station-wide memory/CPU soak needing its own recorded baseline and a live station (plan.html:371).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §22 is declared `implementable` again (plan.html:369) and §26 is declared to wait on it (plan.html:29), yet the only open followup queues §24, §28, §29, §26 and §27 and never §22 (plan.html:474).
